ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, board members, and every UBO against: (i) the SECO consolidated Swiss sanctions list and Embargo Act ordinances; (ii) the UN Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN list and the 50% ownership rule due to USD clearing and Stripe/PayPal exposure; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (v) UK OFSI consolidated list; (vi) domestic criminal records, civil litigation databases, and media/vigilance screening. PEP status is obtained via the notarized statutory declaration, business-relationship questionnaire, and an automated electronic utility (World-Check/Dow Jones Equivalent); if a PEP is identified, account opening and ongoing monitoring require escalation to senior management and FINMA-compliant beneficial-owner verification; any suspicion automatically requires a suspicious transaction report to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) within 20 working days under AMLA Art. 9.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Company Index), www.zefix.admin.ch, operated by the Federal Commercial Registry Office; the actual filing and name check are executed via the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) using the notarial e-filing portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be rendered in German, French, Italian, or Romansh; Latin script is mandatory and foreign-language letters, diacritics, and transliteration must be certified by a registered translator. The name must contain the mandatory legal suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (alternatively 'SA' or 'Société Anonyme') pursuant to Art. 950 CO and must respect the principle of truth (Art. 954 CO), avoiding any misleading indication of economic purpose or capacity. If a foreign trade name is used in parallel, a certified translation into one Swiss national language must be filed with the registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque (requires prior FINMA banking licence)
Swiss / Switzerland / Confédération suisse (requires prior cantonal and federal authorization under Art. 951-961 CO; only usable if majority Swiss-controlled or substantial Swiss commercial interest)
Trust (requires cantonal authorization; imposes fiduciary-capacity obligations)
Insurance / Assurances / Versicherung (requires insurance supervisory licence)
Fonds / Fondation / Fund (triggers financial supervisory statutes and FINMA scrutiny)
Eidgenössisch / Federal / Confederation (reserved, misleading public-authority connotation)
Group / Holding / Konzern (only permitted if consolidated control exists or name is used as a true umbrella)
Valorem / Fiscal / Tax (misleading implication of tax privileges or official fiscal capacity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Commercial Register of Zug rejects the requested name, the notary receives a written notice with the legal basis. Within 30 days of receipt the applicant may: (i) re-submit an amended name through the notary with a revised deed addendum; or (ii) file an administrative appeal ('Beschwerde') with the Commercial Register Office itself, then within 10 days to the Administration Court of the Canton of Zug, and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court in St. Gallen. During the appeal, the registry may place the proposed name in a provisional hold; a request for an extension of the 30-day name-validity window is granted only upon proof of pending disputes with an opposing trademark holder. The recommended route is to resolve conflicts via a notarized disclaimer or citation to prior-right consent and to re-file concurrently; Zefix search extracts are reissued at each step (fee CHF 20-50).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible but conditional. The AG must maintain an actual registered office and service address in Canton Zug (Art. 621 CO), with a current seat where official notices, tax assessments, and judicial documents are physically received and where the board file is accessible. A pure mail-forwarding P.O. box is invalid; however, a licensed co-working/domiciliation provider in Zug offering physical reception, scan-and-forward services, and meeting rooms satisfies the regulatory standard for an ISIC 5920 digital marketplace with no statutory license. At least one authorized signatory (a natural person) must be domiciled in Switzerland (Art. 718 CO) - typically the Swiss resident director or licensed fiduciary - and the registered address must serve as the seat of real operational control, board minutes, and accounting records. Stripe/PayPal payment processing and cloud-based licensing do not require Swiss substance beyond this, although the Tax Office of Zug scrutinizes substance if the foreign shareholders hold over 50% of the capital.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection: approximately 3% for a low-risk, statutorily unlicensed business model of this type. The commercial registry generally performs documentary oversight only. The Cantonal Tax Office of Zug may conduct a substance questionnaire and a possible visit within the first three fiscal years if the declared expenses or head-office deduction appear artificial; the probability rises to approximately 10% where the company relies upon a virtual office without a Swiss resident director or where base-erosion indicators are detected in VAT or corporate tax filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht), Art. 620 et seq., specifically Art. 621 (Content of Articles), Art. 626 (Minimum capital), Art. 632 (Registered share capital), Art. 634 (Payment of contributions), Art. 635 (Validity of registration), Art. 716 and 716a (Non-transferable board powers), Art. 717 (Duty of diligence); also Federal Act on Commercial Register Registration (e.g. Art. 15 of the Ordinance on the Commercial Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons), operating under the Federal Commercial Register Authority (Federal Office of Justice); final registration is published through the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation including the Articles of Association (Statuts / Statuten), executed before a Swiss notary public, followed by an application for registration on Form ZH/Commercial Register extraction.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Aktiengesellschaft requires minimum registered share capital of CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be effectively paid-in before registration, deposited in cash with a Swiss bank and subject to a blocking/confirmation obligation until the Commercial Register proceeds. Share capital contributions exceeding paid-in minimum may be made in non-cash assets under Art. 628 CO; the deed must fully establish payment and blocking certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1/AG-2026. At the first meeting of the Board of Directors of the company, duly convened, all directors present resolve as follows: The existing Articles of Association and their lawful execution are ratified and incorporated as corporate law instruments. All registered shares of the undertaking are validly issued and allocated in accordance with the capital declaration established in the deed. The registered seat of the company is formally ascertained to be the address stated in the Public Deed of Incorporation, which the Board accepts and adopts as the company's principal place of business. The following natural persons are hereby appointed as officers: the Chairman, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Corporate Secretary, each with authority to execute and file the registration applications. The Board authorizes any one such officer, acting jointly, to appear before the Commercial Register and complete all statutory filings and formalities necessary for entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and authenticate preparatory corporate instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss public notary (notaire public / öffentliche Urkundsperson) located in the chosen canton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: English would be acceptable only when official translation is certified; engage a registered Swiss notary to translate and attest the draft Articles of Association, shareholder incl. ownership schedule, bank blocking confirmation, and mandate documents. The deed must include true name and seat, share category and nominal value, number of shares, constitution of capital, and initial board authority clauses.
required_dossiers: Nationality or identification documents of each founder
Certified passport/identity copies for director and shareholder
Notarized draft Articles of Association in French/German/Italian
Declaration of non-disqualification for each director
Original banking evidence of capital deposit blocking
Proof of company address and posterity if relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary may refuse to certify if articles violate mandatory law; remedy is to amend articles in conformity (e.g. introduce strictly qualified share classes), re-certify by the same notary, or request a pre-consultation from the Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a blocked share capital account with a Swiss-regulated bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A bank licensed by FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority), operating in the canton of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital contribution escrow account in the company's name, deposit the minimum paid-in amount of CHF 50,000, and direct the bank to issue an irrevocable blocking certificate. The bank must confirm that funds are at free disposal exclusively for capital payment and cannot be withdrawn until the Commercial Register entry is completed.
required_dossiers: Corporate constitutive draft and Articles of Association
Founder ID and tax proof (U.S. tax form/no U.S. status as applicable)
Beneficial owner declaration under AML
Bank's own account opening forms
USD Currency declaration if transfers come from outside Switzerland
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines due to AML or source-of-wealth deficiency, remedy is to engage a second FINMA-licensed bank or a Swiss single/multifamily office that accepts corporate founders; if required payment originates from a non-transparent jurisdiction, provide BR/ passport and asset statement to satisfy beneficial ownership verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public at the jurisdiction of the company's registered seat; simultaneously record before cantonal commercial register office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the formal constitutive meeting. All founders or their attorneys must appear before the notary, declare consent to the Articles, and sign the deed. The notary shall read the deed, certify presence, and formally acknowledge the capital certificate. The notarial process also triggers appointment of the Board of Directors and confirms the first corporate acts.
required_dossiers: Notarially signed draft public deed
Founders' original identification documents
Power of attorney in notarial form where applicable
Bank blocking confirmation certificate
List of directors and officers with signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary finds a defect in the capital deposit or the composition of authorised capital, the legal remedy is to amend the deed and re-execute if necessary; the notary provides a formal list of objections and a recommended conventional cure within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit electronic application to the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton (Handelsregisteramt) where the seat is located; filings are submitted via the Swiss Commercial Register platform (web application based on the unified software of the Federal Office of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After deed execution, the officers transmit the registration request through the cantonal Commercial Register and receive an archiving reference. The office verifies lawful name, lawful capital, lawful signature of directors, and publication requirements. A single cantonal fee applies and is paid after invoicing.
required_dossiers: Complete notarial deed
Certified signatures of all directors
Exact purpose of the company compatible with statutory permissive activity
Declaration of capital payment and blocking release
Articles signed by of counsel or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an interim query (provisional refusal), company and notary must file an explanatory brief within 30 days; if the defect concerns company name (Art. 46 OR), proposed alternative name or consent of trademark holder is required; otherwise appeal to the supreme cantonal authority within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive certificate of incorporation, obtain UID and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (companies entry) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (EStV / FTA) for UID and VAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration entry is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, the registry issues the official incorporation excerpt. The tax office automatically assigns a UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) if turnover threshold is met; otherwise apply via the federal e-portal. Multi-level VAT-registering is mandatory if global expected taxable turnover is above CHF 100,000.
required_dossiers: Extract of Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug)
UID registration form
VAT registration form (if applicable)
Bank confirmation of account type
Power of attorney for tax representatives if non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is wrong or delayed, (i) submit an online correction via the FTA UID portal; (ii) if the Commercial Register entry lacks issued SAFE-AFT or UID, contact the FTA Data & Organization service directly to activate resend within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No cantonal industrial permit applies to pure digital audio licensing and online sample subscription; the relevant general authority remains the cantonal Trade Inspectorate (Gewerbeaufsicht / Inspection du travail) and municipal commercial registry obligation for virtual/business activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – the target activity is a non-manufacturing digital service; only the general undertaking permit (Handelsregister compliance) applies. If the company adds studio recording or mastering, it must notify the cantonal authority for trade/business operation, but no CH-specific operational industrial licence is necessary.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / UFAM)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity of royalty-free music licensing and audio sample subscription is not an Annex category under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV/OEIE). No EIA certificate is required; the only condition is compliance with general environmental liability and waste provisions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure digital licensing; if ancillary office/ICT operations exist, comply with Swiss federal waste prevention (Ordinance DVS/OLED) requiring separate disposal of e-waste and data storage hardware, and limit emissions from offices to general low-discharge combustion standard (< 1.2 g/kg NOx for heating plants). No VOCs or wastewater process thresholds apply because no chemical/physical processing occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For office-only use (no factory or sound stage): obtain local fire safety confirmation from the municipal fire inspector (based on building code VKF/AEAI), ensure structural load capacity for installed computer racks/servers, and carry out the occupational health checklist under SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) requiring ergonomic workstation assessment, first-aid provisions, and fire extinguisher compliance. If premises exceed standard office worker capacities, cantonal labour law clearance may apply under Art. 20 of the Swiss Labour Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV / AFC), Bern; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporation of Aktiengesellschaft (AG) via notarial deed and entry in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) of the canton of domicile. 2. Automatic assignment of the Swiss UID (Unternehmensidentifikationsnummer / IDE / IDI) to the registered company by the UID service; the UID serves as the unified identification number for tax and statistical purposes. 3. Submission of the VAT registration form to the FTA if the company is subject to Swiss VAT (expected taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold before commencement of activity). 4. For cantonal and communal tax purposes, separate registration with the cantonal tax administration occurs automatically through the commercial register notification. Non-resident shareholders or directors are permitted; no additional federal tax registration type is required for a foreign-owned AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election. The AG is inherently governed by entity-level taxation at the federal, cantonal and communal levels. Relief mechanisms include the tax-neutral reorganisation provisions (VU 2020) and the possibility of obtaining an advance tax ruling (Vorbescheid / ruling fiscal) from the competent cantonal tax authority to confirm application of tax laws to specific facts. Switzerland also implements ATAD-driven hybrid mismatch rules preventing double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion; no elective transparency regime exists for AGs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss VAT (Value Added Tax, Mehrwertsteuer / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover from supplies and own-use (for resident legal entities; non-established suppliers are generally subject to VAT registration without a threshold if their supplies are taxable in Switzerland and no exemption applies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping. B2B e-invoicing is not mandatory in the private sector, but electronic invoices are accepted if they comply with the Swiss VAT Act requirements on authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility. Mandatory e-invoicing (Peppol BIS 3.0) applies for invoicing the federal administration under public procurement rules. For all Swiss payment slips, the QR-bill format is mandatory, requiring a QR reference or ISO 11649 reference, but this does not constitute fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For tangible goods, zero-rating applies when goods are physically exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination and the export is evidenced by a confirmed customs export declaration (AUS-2 / redevance d'exportation). For intellectual and digital services (e.g., royalty-free stock music licensing), Swiss VAT is not chargeable when the supply is deemed to take place outside Switzerland: in B2B transactions at the recipient's business establishment and in B2C transactions at the consumer's habitual residence. Such services are 'zero-rated' or outside Swiss VAT scope with the supplier entitled to input VAT deduction where connected to exported supplies. The supplier must obtain and retain adequate documentary evidence of the recipient's foreign location, including recipient VAT number, IP/geolocation data, client contracts, invoices and payment/bank settlement records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing transport to foreign territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Foreign Currency / payment proof) evidencing actual international payment flow
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA may retroactively reclaim the zero rating and disallow input VAT deduction if the exporter fails to provide conclusive proof of export, recipient foreign status, or receipt of proceeds within the expected commercial timeframe. Interest runs from the original due date of the VAT. Intentional VAT evasion is subject to a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; negligent tax shortfall is fined up to 10% of the tax omitted. Fraudulent or unnecessary claim of export zero-rating or refunds also triggers criminal prosecution and clawback of the full beneficial amount plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, acting in coordination with the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange-rate regime. Switzerland maintains an open capital account with no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements, and no restrictions on the free movement of capital or services under the Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital and the Free Movement of Services. Current-account and capital-account transactions, including dividend distributions, loan repayments, royalty payments, and equity injections, may be executed freely in any convertible currency. Cross-border profit remittance is subject only to ordinary corporate tax settlement and, for dividends only, Swiss anticipatory withholding tax at 35%, which may be reduced under the applicable double tax treaty. Royalty and licence fees paid to non-residents are generally not subject to Swiss withholding tax. The practical impediments to convertibility are therefore confined to bank-level anti-money-laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) source-of-funds verification, not to foreign-exchange permission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation requirement for export receipts. The Swiss AG may retain foreign-currency earnings offshore or hold them on Swiss bank accounts in any denomination without conversion duties. The only statutory burden is statistical: Swiss residents holding cross-border assets, liabilities, or payment flows may be required to report balance-of-payments and direct investment data to the SNB, typically triggered by SNB surveys or where aggregate cross-border transactions exceed approximately CHF 1 million in a reporting period or where foreign direct investment participation exceeds 10% of the AG's share capital. These reporting duties are analytical and non-restrictive; they do not require any surrender or conversion of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF, EUR, USD multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account for share capital deposit
Operational Account (CHF current account with SEPA/EUR clearing capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary treasury rail; Low as the primary transactional account. Swiss-licensed fintech banks and neo-banks offer partially digital onboarding, but for a non-resident-owned AG with foreign directors, enhanced due diligence and physical or notarised identification are generally still required. Offshore digital EMI licenses (UK FCA e-money, EU PSD2 e-money institutions) are lawful to use as collection conduits but are not supervised by FINMA, do not qualify as 'banks' for Swiss deposit-protection or withholding-tax purposes, and may cause acceptance friction with Swiss correspondent banks on inbound wires. The recommended architecture is a FINMA-supervised Tier-1 Swiss bank as the principal treasury account, with Stripe, PayPal, or an offshore EMI strictly limited to marketplace settlement collection and swept daily or weekly into the CHF operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss commercial banks generally mandate physical appearance by the authorised signatories and ultimate beneficial owners, or a personal introduction by a Swiss-regulated fiduciary (Treuhänder) performing face-to-face identity verification. Fully remote corporate onboarding is available only in narrow cases, such as existing bank relationships or Swiss-resident directors authenticating via certified e-ID. For a non-resident-owned Swiss AG, the standard underwriting path requires at least one in-person meeting in Switzerland with a compliance officer; alternatively, the board may appoint a Swiss resident authorised signatory with treasury power of attorney while the foreign directors execute the account-opening resolution. Private banks typically require an interview, either onsite or via secure video with notarised biometric identity documents, to assess source of wealth, business model, and expected payment flows for a low-risk digital audio-licensing enterprise.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner without a Swiss nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of passport and proof of residence; Tier-1 bank reference letter from an existing financial institution; notarised board resolution authorising account opening; signed Swiss AMLA Form A (beneficial owner declaration); source-of-wealth statement; and, where applicable, a Swiss regulated fiduciary introduction or a Swiss resident authorised signatory with documented treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency low-value marketplace collections via Stripe and PayPal
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial licensing agreements and end-user terms; monthly marketplace payout reports; Stripe and PayPal settlement statements; historical bank statements of the marketplace settlement accounts; a business-model memorandum describing royalty-free stock-music licensing and subscription mechanics; and a projected cash-flow forecast demonstrating legitimate commercial purpose and expected transaction patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty flows and potential substance or beneficial-ownership scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed IP assignment and licence agreements; arm's-length transfer pricing documentation; a Swiss advance tax ruling confirming royalty treatment; substance evidence comprising a Swiss registered office lease, board meeting minutes, payroll records for Swiss-based staff, and a group organisational chart locating operational decision-making in Switzerland; and a global compliance file demonstrating no artificial round-tripping or treaty-shopping.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A compliant capital injection is executed via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from the shareholder's bank to the AG's Swiss Capital Escrow Account in CHF, EUR, or USD. The payment reference must identify the purpose as paid-in share capital (Aktienkapital) using the appropriate Swiss payment reason code for equity contribution. The receiving Swiss bank will require a statutory declaration of source of funds; where the shareholder is a legal entity, it must provide certified corporate resolutions, register extracts, and authority documents demonstrating the signatory power for the injection. No exchange-control authorisation is required. However, the transaction may appear in SNB balance-of-payments and direct investment reporting where the foreign participation exceeds 10% of the AG's share capital or the transaction exceeds the SNB's statistical thresholds (commonly CHF 1 million). For capital contributions above CHF 1 million, the Swiss bank may additionally require an updated Form A, the notarial deed covering the share capital increase, and confirmation that the minimum paid-in capital requirement has been satisfied.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements use the Swiss SIC retail payment system and SEPA credit-transfer rails for domestic and euro-area payments; SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with full structured payment details for high-value international settlements; SWIFT MT202/COV for correspondent-bank cover transfers where interbank clearing is required; and documentary instruments such as irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 and documentary collections where physical distribution of audio products, print-on-demand merchandise, or master-licence deliverables requires proof of payment. The AG should maintain an EUR-denominated account at the Swiss bank or a SEPA member institution to avoid conversion friction on marketplace payouts, and should configure automated daily sweeps from Stripe and PayPal settlement balances into the CHF treasury account. SWIFT gpi tracking is recommended on all material outbound wires to provide real-time status, reduce AML-related delays, and evidence legitimate purpose in the licensing of audio content to licensors and contributors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC foreign-exchange forward contracts (outright and flex forwards) with FINMA-supervised bank counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (EUR-CHF and USD-CHF) for medium-term cash-flow matching of subscription and royalty receivables
FX options, including plain-vanilla options, collars, and zero-premium structures, for risk-limited hedging
Multi-currency account and natural-offset hedging through matched EUR/USD receipts and CHF disbursements

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible only for illiquid or restricted currencies and are unnecessary for CHF, USD, and EUR, which are fully convertible; Swiss banks generally decline NDFs for major convertible currencies on operational and accounting grounds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) and profit appropriation at the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a government filing; AGM minutes retained in the Minute Book at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM leaves the annual accounts unapproved and renders the company defective as to corporate organs; a 60-day formal cure notice from the commercial register or court may be followed by court-ordered dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements, and the ordinary auditor's report if issued, with the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton (e.g., Zug)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder with a set cure period (typically 30 days); administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; persistent non-compliance may trigger official enforcement or involuntary dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return including the capital-tax calculation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (competent for federal, cantonal and municipal taxes; Swiss Federal Tax Administration receives the federal share)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by 31 March of the year following the tax year for a 31 December year-end; most cantons grant an extension to 30 September upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default estimate and assessment, late-filing surcharge, default interest of approximately 3-5% per annum, enforcement/attachment measures, and penalties for negligent or intentional tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return and settlement (annual or quarterly, as approved by ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after the end of the VAT tax period; for an annual period ending 31 December, by 1 March of the following year; for quarterly periods, 60 days after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of about 4.5% per annum, reminder fees, procedural fines under the Swiss VAT Act (ordinarily up to CHF 8,000), and additional penalty assessments for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updating and annual confirmation of the shareholder register (Aktienbuch) and beneficial-owner records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records at the registered office; required by law to be available for inspection; no annual government filing in Switzerland
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty upon each share transfer; recommended full year-end consistency check by 30 June after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete Aktienbuch suspends shareholder rights until registration and exposes directors to liability; correction is required before transfers are recognized.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit is required if the AG exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million; net turnover above CHF 40 million; annual average more than 250 full-time employees. Listed companies, issuers of debt instruments and regulated financial intermediaries are always subject to ordinary audit. Other companies are subject to limited audit unless they validly opt out with unanimous shareholder consent and no more than 10 employees; a royalty-free stock-music licensing AG normally qualifies for the opting-out exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 957-963b OR) for statutory single-entity annual accounts; Swiss GAAP FER is the recognized local GAAP for true-and-fair presentation; IFRS is mandatory for listed issuers and permitted for annual or consolidated statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland imposes no annual UBO declaration to a public register for a private AG. The Aktienbuch must be updated without delay upon every share transfer; the board obtains written declarations from shareholders and beneficial owners on each transfer and, as best practice, annual signed confirmations each balance-sheet year. Bearer shares of non-listed companies have been converted to registered shares; any residual bearer-shareholder records remain inspectable. Shareholders may be required to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner before voting rights and dividends are granted, and the directors must ensure the true ownership position coincides with the annual accounts' share-capital note.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Aktienbuch (Register of Members), kept at the registered office
Register of Directors and corporate organs (dossier of appointments and signatures)
Minute Book of shareholders' and board meetings
Beneficial-owner and residual bearer-shareholder records (UBO register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450-3,500 (CHF 400-3,000) typical annual domiciliation / registered-agent service for an AG in Zug, Zurich or Geneva
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 when the opting-out exemption is available; otherwise USD 4,000-15,000 for a limited audit and USD 15,000-50,000+ for an ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax (direkte Bundessteuer) at 8.5% on after-tax profit, equal to 7.83% on the pre-tax base, plus Zug cantonal and communal corporate income tax; combined statutory rate for a Zug-resident AG is approximately 11.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in Switzerland. Recurring reliefs for a music-licensing AG: (i) participation relief on substantial dividend income; (ii) Zug Licence Box exempting 90% of qualifying IP/royalty income from cantonal taxation, with the federal-law minimum box rate applicable; (iii) Zug R&D super-deduction allowing 150% of eligible in-house music-software and sample-library R&D costs; (iv) effective federal burden reduced to 7.83% pre-tax; single-digit effective combined rates typically achievable for qualifying licence-box income.
